target.title: fix(browser): keep tab reachability retry delay abortable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelling a browser tab operation during the reachability retry delay would wait the full delay before responding to the cancellation.

`ensureBrowserRunning` used `new Promise(setTimeout)` for the 250ms retry delay between reachability probes. When the request `AbortSignal` fired during this delay, the function waited the entire `TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS` before calling `signal.throwIfAborted()`, adding unnecessary latency to cancellation-sensitive callers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry delay now uses `sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal)` which rejects immediately when the signal fires, so the caller is notified of the cancellation during the delay rather than after it.

Related prior art: #108561 (discord gateway READY retry abortSignal), #108408 (feishu retry abortSignal propagation).

## User Impact

Browser tab operations (close, focus, select) cancelled during the 250ms reachability retry window respond to user cancellation up to 250ms faster.

## Evidence

### Scope

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Head | `eac9fd9a2f5` |
| Files | `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts` (+4/−5) · `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` (+1/−1) |
| Net | +5 / −6 across 2 files |

### Production change (behavior)

```ts
// Before
await new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, RETRY_DELAY_MS); });
signal?.throwIfAborted();

// After
await sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal);
```

### Real-timer timing proof

A standalone Node.js script (`scripts/proof-109536-abort-timing.mjs`) compares the two patterns with real `performance.now()` timers and a real `AbortController`. Each scenario is run 5 times with the abort signal firing 50ms into the 250ms retry delay:

```
--- BEFORE (old code) ---
  Run 1: 250.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 2: 250.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 3: 250.3 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 4: 251.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 5: 250.2 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)

--- AFTER (new code: sleepWithAbort) ---
  Run 1: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 2: 50.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 3: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 4: 51.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 5: 50.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
```

- **BEFORE**: consistently ~250ms — always waits the full retry delay before noticing the abort.
- **AFTER**: consistently ~50ms — rejects as soon as the abort signal fires, eliminating up to 200ms of unnecessary wait.

The same abort-propagation invariant is additionally covered by the fake-timer unit test at `tabs.test.ts:345`.

### Local gates (touched surface)

| Gate | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` | **22 passed** / 1 file |

### Proof

The existing test "does not retry or mutate after cancellation during the retry delay" covers this scenario: it advances past the first reachability check, aborts the signal, then verifies no reachability retry occurred. With `sleepWithAbort`, the abort is detected immediately during the delay rather than after it expires, and the error message changes from `"cancelled"` (from `throwIfAborted`) to `"aborted"` (from `sleepWithAbort`).

Real-timer proof confirms the timing improvement holds with real wall-clock timers, not only with fake timers.
